definition.name: Motor overload relay
definition.description: Motor current trips an auxiliary control contact. It only stops the motor if the control circuit uses that contact correctly.

terminals.purpose: Incoming side of motor-current sensing path 1–2. This teaching overload measures the path current; its trip opens 95–96 rather than these power paths. The contactor must remove power through the wired control circuit.

Outgoing side of motor-current sensing path 1–2. This teaching overload measures the path current; its trip opens 95–96 rather than these power paths. The contactor must remove power through the wired control circuit.

Incoming side of motor-current sensing path 3–4. This teaching overload measures the path current; its trip opens 95–96 rather than these power paths. The contactor must remove power through the wired control circuit.

Incoming side of motor-current sensing path 5–6. This teaching overload measures the path current; its trip opens 95–96 rather than these power paths. The contactor must remove power through the wired control circuit.

Outgoing side of motor-current sensing path 5–6. This teaching overload measures the path current; its trip opens 95–96 rather than these power paths. The contactor must remove power through the wired control circuit.

Normally closed overload control-contact pair 95–96. It opens after the represented overload trips. Place it in the coil permission path; a trip cannot stop an unrelated motor circuit automatically. Reset after removing the overload cause.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The enclosure supports and separates functional parts. This original teaching model is representative equipment, not a manufacturer drawing.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: The cover limits access to internal connections. Opening it here is a virtual inspection operation.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: Metal clamps establish connections to individual conductors. The circuit engine connects terminal IDs, not the apparent proximity of 3D wires.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: Mounting hardware supports the equipment. Screws, rail clips and glands are modelled separately from electrical connections.

parts.name: Thermal protection
parts.purpose: A thermal element responds to heating or sustained excess current. Timing is illustrative here; it is not a manufacturer trip curve.

parts.name: Switching contacts
parts.purpose: Contacts either connect or separate their terminal pairs. Their position is linked to the simulation state, including normally open and normally closed functions.

parts.name: Operating mechanism
parts.purpose: The mechanism translates a handle, button, coil or control demand into an operating state.
